newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia's Aviakor plane maker plans cut staff.
newsitem.headline: Russia's Aviakor plane maker plans cut staff.

text.p: Russia's AO Aviakor aircraft manufacturer plans to cut 2,000 jobs because it has insufficient orders for production of Tupolev-154 passenger jets, a senior company official said on Wednesday.
Aviakor Deputy Chief Executive Vladimir Ryzhkov told Reuters altogether about 8,000 workers out of 13,000 have been laid off on short pay until next January.
Of these 8,000, "we have informed the Federal Employement Service about plans to sack about 2,000 people," Ryzhkov said by telephone from the company's headquarters in Samara, central Russia.
He said Aviakor had not sold a single Tu-154 so far this year. In 1995 the company delivered nine Tu-154 jets compared with 78 in 1981.

"We have 28 contracts, but customers do not pay for aircraft," Ryzhkov said, adding that the plant was completing assembly of three Tu-154s for Czech, Ukrainian and Siberian airlines. One Tu-154 jet costs $13 million.
He also said that Aviakor hoped to get financial help from the Samara regional authorities later this year.
"Local authorities promised us 200 billion roubles ($36.9 million) for production of a new Tupolev-334 jet for 1997-98," he said.
Aviakor also modernises Tu-154s, producing a Tu-154-100 version with improved engines, a new design cabin and upgraded avionics. However, the plant does not have orders for this plane yet.
All 28,000 staff at Samara-based AO Aviastar, which produces Tupolev Tu-204 passenger jets, are on leave on reduced pay until November 1, a company official told Reuters last week.
Aviastar stopped work on August 21 because power supplies had been cut off because it had not paid its electricity bills.
